subject: Request: critical patch escrow & remediation evidence
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@orbishealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: critical patch escrow & remediation evidence

Connor —

Thanks for taking this. Orbis is preparing for our SOC 2 refresh and our security team needs a compact evidence packet to satisfy the vendor assessment. Can you provide the following by 2027-05-15?

- A signed attestation covering remediation SLAs and observed remediation dates for the two CVEs called out below (we'll need a PDF with a signature block): CVE-2027-0421 (Critical) and CVE-2026-9987 (High).
- The vulnerability management playbook (scan cadence, authenticated vs unauthenticated scans, triage and patch windows).
- Export of the last 12 weeks of authenticated scan results (CSV preferred) and proof that critical items were escalated to on-call (pager/incident ids or ticket refs).
- Confirmation of your SLA for critical/important CVEs and whether you maintain a critical-patch escrow or TPA arrangement for customers requiring additional assurance.

If you have a short attestation template we can accept a signed PDF copy, that will be fastest. Also confirm whether you can include evidence of the fix dates for CVE-2027-0421 and CVE-2026-9987 (we need calendar dates and the internal ticket ids).

Appreciate it — if you prefer, we can schedule a 20-minute call to walk through.

—Maria
Maria Lopez
Senior InfoSec Manager, Vendor Risk
Orbis Health

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Maria —

Thanks for the clear list. I've started compiling materials; attaching our vulnerability playbook excerpt and the authenticated scan export for the last 12 weeks. A couple quick notes:

- We can provide a signed attestation PDF. I'll draft it and loop in Evelyn (Director, Engineering) to sign.
- Our operational SLAs (current, company policy): Critical (P0): initial mitigation/patch or compensating control within 24 hours, remediation verification within 72 hours. High (P1): mitigation/patch within 7 days. Medium (P2): 30 days. These are enforced by our SRE and on-call rotation.
- Scan cadence: weekly authenticated scans (credentialed), daily unauthenticated quick scans on public surfaces, and quarterly third-party penetration tests.
- We do not currently escrow binaries with a TPA for customers, but we maintain a documented critical-patch procedure with defined escalation to a 24/7 on-call and will provide a signed letter describing that process. If Orbis requires a third-party escrow, we can discuss options (we have done limited TPA arrangements for enterprise customers).

Attached: vulnerability_playbook_v1.pdf; scan_export_20270425.csv (redacted ticket ids in CSV replaced with internal ref tokens, full ticket ids can be provided under NDA).

Can you confirm whether the attestation needs to be notarized, or whether a director-signed PDF is sufficient?

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com

Connor —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the playbook and scan export. A couple follow-ups so we can close this in our tooling: 

1) For CVE-2027-0421 (Critical) we need the precise remediation date and the internal ticket id that shows the patch rollout and verification. Can you provide the internal id (not necessarily the full commit hash) and the date the change reached production?
2) For CVE-2026-9987 (High) same ask — date and ticket id.
3) The attestation needs to be a director-signed PDF (no notarization).
4) Please also include a note about whether your automated patch pipeline includes canary and rollback windows (we require evidence of rollback capability for critical fixes).

If it's easier, please forward the attestation template and we'll confirm it meets Orbis requirements.

—Maria

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Attestation: Redwood Inference CVE remediation commitments (signed)

Maria —

Please find our signed attestation attached (cve_attestation_signed.pdf). Summary and direct answers below for your intake system: 

- CVE-2027-0421 (Critical): Remediation implemented to production on 2027-04-18 UTC. Internal ticket: RDW-SEC-2074. Verification of fix and post-deploy validation completed 2027-04-19 UTC.
- CVE-2026-9987 (High): Patch deployed to production on 2027-03-29 UTC. Internal ticket: RDW-SEC-1906. Verification completed 2027-03-30 UTC.

Operational commitments (excerpt):
- SLAs: Critical (P0): initial mitigation within 24 hours, patch & verification within 72 hours. High (P1): remediation within 7 days. Medium (P2): 30 days.
- Scan cadence: weekly authenticated scans (credentialed, internal VM images), daily unauthenticated surface scans, monthly dependency scans for third-party libs, quarterly external pentests.
- Patch deployment process: staged rollout with canary (5% initial), 30-minute health observation, progressive rollout to 100% if metrics stable; automatic rollback triggers on defined error/latency thresholds.
- Evidence retention: scan results and remediation tickets retained 3 years; audit logs retained 12 months in our access-controlled S3 bucket (kms key: rw-inference-logs-prod).
- Escrow/TPA: We do not escrow binaries by default. For customers requiring escrow, we have a commercial option involving a vetted TPA; we are open to discussing on a case-by-case basis.

Attachments included: cve_attestation_signed.pdf (Director-signed), and a reference pointer to the playbook and scan export that Connor provided. If Orbis needs a redacted ticket trail (full internal ticket ids rather than the tokenized references in the CSV), we can share under an executed NDA or via an encrypted artifact bundle.

Signed,

Evelyn Hart
Director of Engineering, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
